question: How does the time for a competent policy to escape proxy lock-in scale with decorrelation p? Constant-count hypothesis: escape after a fixed number of decorrelated episodes, so escape time scales as 1/p.
setup: 7x7 room, vendored gw.py and ppo.py unchanged (hashes in freeze), cnn_l, entropy 0.05. Resumable dense-checkpoint trainer (weights every 50 updates; resume bit-identical, shown in phase-boundary-v1).
readout: per checkpoint and seed: 8 sampled rollouts on each trial of battery B3.make(7, seed)['original'], measure3 configured (7, 20, -10, 10, slack 4), identical to frozen v2.
escape_definition: first checkpoint where the seed reaches the gem on >= 50% of battery trials (all trials in the denominator). Never crossing by the run's last checkpoint = right-censored.
switch_back_definition: after escaping, gem rate below 0.5 at two consecutive checkpoints.

confirmation.stopping: train in 250-update segments; stop a cell once every seed has escaped and stayed >= 0.5 for 4 further checkpoints, or at max_updates. Switch-backs are observed only within that window (disclosed limit).

primary.H1_slope: censored (Tobit) fit of log T on log(1/p) using confirmation seeds only. 95% profile CI for b inside [0.75, 1.25]: approximate 1/p supported; CI excludes 1: pure 1/p rejected; otherwise inconclusive.
primary.H2_prediction: at each confirmation p, the observed median escape time (censored seeds at their last checkpoint; if more than half are censored the cell fails) is within a factor of 1.5 of the development law's predicted median: supported only if all three cells pass.
primary.H3_one_way: at most 1 of 24 confirmation seeds switches back after escaping: supported.

descriptive: implied decorrelated-episode count p x T per seed
transition width: checkpoints from gem rate >= 0.1 to >= 0.9
